questions.q: A writer puts a title before each scene announcing what will happen in it. What's the intended effect, in Brecht's terms?
choices: To give the actor a super-objective
To shift attention from "what happens next?" to "how and why does it happen?"
To build suspense toward an obligatory scene
questions.explain: Knowing the outcome frees the audience to examine causes, as in Mother Courage.

questions.q: Why is "alienation effect" a misleading translation of Verfremdungseffekt?
choices: He wanted to make the familiar look strange so it could be seen freshly, not to push the audience away
Brecht wanted to repel the audience
questions.explain: "Estrangement" or "defamiliarization" is closer to his aim.

questions.q: In Brecht's table, dramatic theatre links scenes so one makes the next. What does epic theatre do?
choices: Treats each scene for itself, moving in curves and jumps
questions.explain: Episodic structure is a deliberate challenge to Aristotle's causal unity.

questions.q: What was Brecht's main objection to the Aristotelian model?
choices: Identification and catharsis left audiences passive, feeling events were inevitable
questions.explain: He wanted audiences to leave asking why things happened and whether they could change.

questions.q: Which of these is a Brechtian technique?
choices: A secret letter locked in a letterbox
Visualizing a character with eyes closed
A song that interrupts the action and comments on it
questions.explain: Songs, titles, visible machinery and actors who show the character all make the familiar strange.

questions.q: What happened after Mother Courage's 1941 premiere in Zurich?
choices: Audiences condemned Courage as a profiteer, as Brecht hoped
Many saw Courage as a tragic suffering mother, and Brecht revised the play to make her less sympathetic
questions.explain: It's the classic case of audiences identifying despite the theory.

questions.q: A documentary opens by telling you the outcome, then shows the system that produced it. Whose logic is this closest to?
questions.explain: Telling the end first and examining causes is epic-theatre thinking.

ideas: Theatre should make the familiar strange, so the audience sees it freshly and judges it.
Tell the audience what will happen before each scene, so they watch how and why instead of what next.
An actor should show the character, as if quoting them, rather than disappear into the role.
Each scene should stand for itself rather than one scene making the next.
